newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mildly lower on Saturday as profit-taking thwarted the recently red hot market's attempt to push above the 9,000-point barrier, brokers said.
The weighted index pushed briefly above 9,000 to an intra-day high of 9,021.87 in early trade, but lost steam later in the session and closed 0.54 percent or 48.30 points lower at 8,833.83.
Turnover was a hectic T$178 billion in Saturday's abbreviated session.

The stock market, in a rally that analysts said has been fuelled more by pyschological bullishness than tangible changes in Taiwan's economic fundamentals, has gained more than 700 points in June -- even after Saturday's setback.
Brokers said the downturn was a temporary correction that was unlikely to impede the market's recent momentum.
"It is normal for selling pressure to emerge after the drastic gains the market has enjoyed in the past three weeks," said Lin Long-hsien, senior analyst for United Securities.
"But I don't see the overall uptrend changing just because of today," Lin said.
The trend-setting electronics sector, which has driven the recent bull run and is regarded widely as the motor of Taiwan's export-driven economy, lost 1.22 percent on Saturday.
Chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, whose share price has soared since announcing a mammoth T$400 billion wafter project in April, eased T$2 to T$108.
Chipmaker Mosel Vitelic also dropped T$2 to T$82.

Brokers said investors largely ignored the government's late-Friday announcement of a modest annual rise in May export orders and Saturday's late-session announcement of stronger than expected industrial output growth for May.
